proof_steps.label: remark:endpoint-tail-necessity
proof_steps.notes: The source endpoint probability limit entails sℓ times the strict upper tail tending to zero. An interior finite site family counts at least a constant times sℓ points with an admissible outgoing east step inside the region. Its large-weight probability has the exact independent product form. A strict one-step witness uses the source collected-start convention and the fixed support score. The independent client supplies the endpoint probability premise from the actual endpoint theorem.

proof_steps.label: remark:general-aspect-heavy-tail
proof_steps.notes: The global cap uses the printed cutoff and retains the k^p correction. The conditional off-flat coarse result constructs the same actual first dyadic characteristic exponents, minimizers and record set. An eventual power bound for all indices applies at k−j, including when that predecessor is not a record. The coarse mesh is at most w^γ/2. A closed block has at most 17 w^(1+γ) sites, so at threshold w the cap failure probability is at most 17 E[(W⁺)^p] w^(1+γ−p) for p>2 and p>1+γ. This tends to zero uniformly in the eligible coarse parameters, and the same fixed capped trials have probability at least q₀/2 and are jointly independent. The improved scale bound remains a premise. The named heavy lemma retains the cubic regime.

proof_steps.label: remark:general-aspect-excess
proof_steps.notes: The excess estimate proves the actual two-power upper bound with one positive constant at real exponent p>2. The precise little-o threshold characterizes the displayed envelope. The source aspect ratio ensures feasible eventual exponents are greater than one. The final gamma is one plus the parameter specified in the source.

Uniform convergence of the shapes on the closed unit segment gives a common derivative limit and passes the first-order remainder to the original profile. The local statement and its open-quadrant consequence are conditional. Availability of the premise remains unestablished.

proof_steps.notes: On the top flat segment the crossing weight M n equals the shape level term. The positive crossing allowance gives the strict near-optimal inequality whenever the same path satisfies the strip test. The cited exports identify the flat-set and level conventions.

proof_steps.notes: For a fixed finite-width signed strip, almost surely at each fixed signed start level all sufficiently long confined up-right paths have weight strictly below M times their length. Independent levels each have uniformly positive chance of having no top vertex. The usable level is strictly before the terminal level of any sufficiently long path, so it supplies a collected strictly subtop site.

proof_steps.notes: The applications substitute the exact moment powers and thresholds. The explicit staircase exponent includes the log-scale correction described by the draft in the later calculation.

proof_steps.label: remark:attachment-moment-threshold

With integrable W⁻, the elementary first-moment tail test gives t P(W⁻>t)→0 by bounding it with E[W⁻ 1{W⁻>t}], so m P(W⁻>T)→0 when m=O(T). The proof explains its own polynomial decay requirement. The possible logarithmic-moment improvement remains conjectural.
